_meta.purpose: Adversarial inputs NOT present in .ufo/waves/round-88/vary-cases.json, each with the verdict the round's declared contract requires and the spec basis. Inputs are the same JSON carrier the counter uses: {"vary": str, "stored": {name: value|list}, "presented": {name: value|list}}.
_meta.freshness_check: Every (vary, stored, presented) tuple below was diffed against all 20 frozen tuples (scripts/../w1/ExecCases/freshness.py, exit 0). No tuple repeats a frozen one.
_meta.expected_is: the round's declared contract (contract.md profile + the local adapter in c88_vary.py's docstring + ExecReader's item: non-string vary or values, non-token members, empty members and empty Vary are refused).
_meta.spec_reading_is: RFC 9111 section 4.1 read strictly, where it differs from the adapter convention.
_meta.quote_provenance: No network GET this seat (no URL named in the item). 'recalled' marks RFC text not re-fetched; ScoutSpec holds the fetched copies.
under_specified: X04, X07, X15: the counter's reference refuses (exit 1) where 4.1/9110 5.2 gives a match/mismatch. contract.md's profile paragraph declares neither rule, so both answers are currently defensible and the frozen population does not contain these shapes.

X13, X17: 4.1's whitespace transformation would call these a match; the profile's byte comparison calls them a mismatch. Mismatch is conformant (MAY-use is permissive) and is what the contract declares.

cases.basis: Vary is a list of field names; the match condition quantifies over nominated fields, so a repeated member adds no extra conjunct. Frozen case 13 covers case-variant duplicates only.
cases.spec_sentence: RFC 9110 12.5.5: "Vary = #( \"*\" / field-name )" (a list, not a multiset of independent conditions)

cases.axis: Vary value that is only OWS
cases.basis: After trimming OWS the member list is a single empty element, which the adapter refuses. Strictly, RFC 9110 5.6.1.1 requires a recipient to parse and ignore empty list elements, and zero nominated fields cannot fail the match rule.
cases.spec_sentence: RFC 9110 5.6.1.1: "a recipient MUST parse and ignore a reasonable number of empty list elements"

cases.basis: Member order is irrelevant: the presence of '*' anywhere in the list fails the match unconditionally, even though the other member is equal. Frozen cases 7/8 only test '*' alone and '*' last.
cases.spec_sentence: "A Vary header field value of \"*\" always fails to match."

cases.axis: request key with a trailing space
cases.spec_reading: mismatch (the nominated field is absent on the presented side) or refusal (the key is not a field name)
cases.basis: 'accept-encoding ' is not a token, so it does not name the nominated field; the nominated field is then absent from the presented request, which the absence sentence makes a mismatch. Refusing the whole payload is also defensible at the adapter, but it discards a decidable match rule and is not declared in contract.md.
cases.spec_sentence: "If a header field is absent from a request, it can only match another request if it is also absent there."

cases.basis: '_' is in tchar, so 'x_kake_token' is a valid field-name token. The frozen set only exercises hyphenated names; a reader that hard-codes /[a-z-]/ fails here.
One field line combines to itself; the combined value is 'gzip'.
cases.spec_sentence: RFC 9110 5.2: combining appends each subsequent field line value "in order, separated by a comma (',') and optional whitespace"

cases.axis: empty JSON array as a field value
cases.basis: An empty array carries zero field lines, i.e. the field is absent from the presented request, so the absence sentence makes it a mismatch. The counter's reference instead refuses the payload; contract.md declares neither rule. Frozen case 19/20 cover wrong scalar types, not an empty array.
cases.spec_sentence: "If a header field is absent from a request, it can only match another request if it is also absent there."

cases.axis: nominated field present only as an empty string on one side
cases.basis: An empty field value is still a present field line: the field exists on the stored side and is absent on the presented side, so the absence sentence is not satisfied. Distinguishes 'present but empty' from 'absent'.
cases.spec_sentence: "If a header field is absent from a request, it can only match another request if it is also absent there."

cases.basis: Both sides are present with byte-identical (empty) values.
cases.spec_sentence: 4.1: the fields match iff one can be transformed to the other; identity needs no transformation

cases.basis: Only the fields nominated by Vary participate. user-agent is not nominated and its difference is irrelevant.
cases.spec_sentence: "... all of the selecting header fields nominated by the Vary header field match ..."

cases.basis: Three lines combine in order with ', ' to 'gzip, br, en'. Frozen case 16 tests two lines only.
cases.spec_sentence: RFC 9110 5.2: "appending each subsequent field line value to the initial field line value in order, separated by a comma (',') and optional whitespace"

cases.axis: HTAB after the list comma in Vary
cases.basis: OWS follows the list comma; HTAB is OWS. Both nominated fields match.
cases.spec_sentence: RFC 9110 5.6.1: list = #element uses OWS around the comma ("#" expansion permits OWS around ',')

cases.axis: value differing only by internal HTAB
cases.spec_reading: match (removing whitespace allowed after a list comma)
cases.basis: The profile compares trimmed values byte-identically and folds no internal whitespace, so the values differ. 4.1's first transformation would permit normalising this; declining reuse is still conformant.
cases.spec_sentence: "adding or removing whitespace, where allowed in the header field's syntax"

cases.spec_reading: invalid_input (or mismatch: the member is not a field-name)
cases.basis: A field-name is a token; DQUOTE is not in tchar, so the member is malformed. Refusal is the adapter convention the frozen cases already use for malformed members (case 15).

cases.axis: two request-map keys differing only in name case
cases.basis: Two keys that differ only in case are two field lines with the same (case-insensitive) field name; 5.2 combines them in order. The counter's reference refuses them as an ambiguous duplicate name, and contract.md declares neither rule. Python dicts preserve insertion order, so the combination is well defined.
cases.spec_sentence: RFC 9110 5.1 "Field names are case-insensitive" + 5.2 combination in order

cases.basis: '*' fails regardless of field content, so the vacuous-match shortcut for empty maps must not fire.
cases.spec_sentence: "A Vary header field value of \"*\" always fails to match."

cases.axis: array with a trailing empty element
cases.spec_reading: match (the empty list element is ignored)
cases.basis: The profile combines to 'gzip, ' then trims to 'gzip,', which differs from 'gzip'. RFC 9110 5.6.1.1 would have the empty element ignored, leaving 'gzip'.
cases.spec_sentence: RFC 9110 5.6.1.1: "a recipient MUST parse and ignore a reasonable number of empty list elements"

cases.basis: OWS around a list member is not part of the field-name, and names are case-insensitive; values are equal.
